## Interpretation Critique — Round 1

**Verdict: REVISE**

The body's headline read is honest and the data supports it: at ep1 both ρ(D, raw log P) = -0.67 [-0.81, -0.44] and ρ(D, ΔG) = -0.27 [-0.42, -0.13] exclude zero (analysis.json verified), the saturation collapse to 98.8% / 99.2% / 99.2% within 0.1 nat at ep2/3/5 is real, and the ep2-onward raw ρ ≈ -0.77 is correctly demoted as a rank-shuffle on near-zero-variance ceiling cells per the project's measurement-validity rule. The positioning vs #460 is fair — the title carries the caveat in plain English ("but only at the one checkpoint before the log-prob saturates at ceiling"), and the Human TL;DR's "How this updates me" honestly flags that ep1 itself might still be overtraining. Three figures load cleanly and the figure annotations (rho values, n=240, CI bounds, saturation fractions, sd, min) match analysis.json verbatim.

But the body has two reproducibility-accuracy bugs and one understatement that REVISE-level changes can fix without disturbing the headline.

### Overclaims

- **"99% of pairs at epoch 2"** (Human TL;DR Takeaways bullet 1, body line 25) — actual fraction at ep2 is **98.75%** (analysis.json `frac_within_0_1_of_zero`). The hero figure correctly shows 98.8%. The "99%" in prose is colloquially close enough but inconsistent with the figure number; either round the figure to 99% or quote 98.8% in prose. Minor.
- **Pirate-captain outlier framing is too narrow** (Result 3, body line 98) — body says "most of the epoch-1 tail involves either pirate-source or pirate-target cells" and "even the dynamic range at ep1 is partly carried by one persona being a geometric outlier." Verified the tail (g < -0.5): 34 cells, of which 21 touch A3. But the off-ceiling pattern at ep1 is **three personas, not one**: A3 (pirate) 13/15 off-ceiling cells, A4 (comedian) 12/15, A5 (villainous mastermind) 10/15. A1 (helpful) and A2 (software engineer) carry 1/15 each. The honest framing is "the three stylistically-distant personas (pirate-captain, stand-up comedian, villainous mastermind) carry the dynamic range at ep1," not "one persona." This is a real strengthening of the caveat, not a weakening — the geometric-outlier concern is broader than one outlier.

### Surprising Unmentioned Patterns

- **Drop-pirate sensitivity is favorable to the headline and should be in the body.** I recomputed length-partial ρ on the ep1 frame dropping all 30 cells touching A3 (either source or target). Result: ρ(D, raw log P) = **-0.656** [from -0.667, essentially unchanged] and ρ(D, ΔG) = **-0.193**, p = 5e-3 [from -0.27]. The ΔG ρ shrinks by ~30% but **still excludes zero at p < 0.01** — the headline survives removing pirate-captain. This is the natural robustness check given the geometric-outlier caveat the body raises; reporting it strengthens the result rather than weakening it. The body raises the outlier concern but doesn't quantify whether the effect survives its removal, which leaves the reader to wonder.
- **The persona-class pattern at ep1 is itself a substantive finding.** A1/A2 (helpful, software engineer — "neutral" personas) are at-ceiling on 14/15 of their off-diagonal cells at ep1; A3/A4/A5 (pirate, comedian, villainous mastermind — "stylized" personas) are at-ceiling on only 2-5/15. So even at ep1, transfer to/from neutral-style targets is saturated; the unsaturated dynamic range that carries the negative ρ lives almost entirely in stylized-persona pairs. Worth a sentence in Result 3.

### Alternative Explanations Not Addressed

- **The "ep1 might itself be overtraining" alternative is named in the Human TL;DR** ("The next question is whether epoch 1 is itself overtraining") but **not surfaced in the structured TL;DR or the Findings prose** — this is the binding interpretive caveat on the result and belongs in the AI-facing TL;DR too, not only in Thomas's voice section. The current Findings prose reads as if ep1 is the natural "before saturation" reference point; in fact ep1 is the lightest checkpoint *this experiment ran*, and 24% off-ceiling at ep1 vs 75% off-ceiling at ep0.5 (hypothetical) could change the ΔG rho substantially. The "How this updates me" caveat needs a peer in the structured TL;DR.
- **The pirate-captain outlier alternative is named but not ruled out quantitatively** — see Surprising Patterns above. Body should report the drop-A3 ρ to show the headline survives.

### Confidence Calibration

- **Stated: MODERATE. Evidence supports: MODERATE.** Single seed, single base model (Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct), single training recipe (varying only epoch count), the real effect resting on ONE unsaturated training level (ep1) with n=240 off-diagonal pairs where the dynamic range is concentrated in 3-of-5 personas. MODERATE is the right call. Don't lower to LOW; don't raise to HIGH.

- **The covariate name in the Reproducibility table is wrong.** Body line 119 says "Length covariate | log(prompt_tokens) per cell". The actual covariate in `scripts/i462_phase5_analyze.py` (line 217-218) is `log(prompt_plus_R_tokens)` — mean per-question prompt + R length, NOT prompt tokens alone. The DataFrame column is named `log_prompt_tokens` in code (a misnomer inherited from #460), but the underlying quantity is prompt + R. The actual bootstrap (`_cluster_bootstrap_partial_spearman` in `i462_phase5_analyze.py`) is **cluster-bootstrap on class_pair** (16 transformation-class pairs like A_A, A_B, ..., D_D — see lines 119-131), NOT a vanilla cell-level resample. Cluster bootstrap on class_pair gives wider CIs because it accounts for within-class-pair cell dependence. - Epoch 1 is already mostly saturated: 75.8% of off-diagonal cells are within 0.1 nat of zero in `analysis.json` — the "unsaturated checkpoint" still has limited dynamic range.

- The epoch-1 finding could be explained by pirate/comedian geometric outliers and source training-rate differences rather than a general divergence-similarity transfer law — add leave-A3/A4 and source/target grouped sensitivity.
